images.archetype: Circular vignette hero v3 — Scaffold B, still-life (non-people hero)
images.alt: A clear glass carafe of water and a small mound of coarse sea salt balanced on a simple scale beside a blood sample tube, in soft morning light.
Share card reading "Sodium Too Low or Too High? Understanding Dysnatremia" with a balance scale of water and salt.

images.archetype: Visual-aid hybrid — side-by-side comparison (simple-figure Scaffold B)
images.section: Patient tab · "What your sodium number really measures" (#what)
images.alt: Three bowls of soup with the same salt: extra water reads low sodium, normal water reads normal, too little water reads high sodium; below, thirst, vasopressin and the kidneys keep the balance.

images.archetype: Biomedical mechanism figure — 4-frame timeline (organ context → magnified cells → injury → protection)
images.section: Patient tab · "Why the hospital corrects it slowly" (#slow); Clinician tab · Mechanism (#md-physiology)
images.alt: Four frames of brain cells: normal; swollen after a sudden fall in sodium; back to normal size after about two days of adaptation; and shrunken with damaged myelin when sodium is raised too fast.

images.archetype: Clinical algorithm — algorithm-generator Mode C (renalcarematters.com house style), portrait
images.section: Clinician tab · "Establish tonicity before anything else" (#md-tonicity)
images.alt: Algorithm: low sodium → measure osmolality, glucose and assay → hypotonic, isotonic or pseudo, or hypertonic categories with what each means.

images.archetype: Clinical algorithm — algorithm-generator Mode C (renalcarematters.com house style), portrait
images.alt: Algorithm from confirmed hypotonic hyponatremia: urine osmolality 100 or less suggests too much water or low solute; above 100, urine sodium 30 or less suggests low effective volume and above 30 suggests SIAD, diuretics, adrenal insufficiency or renal loss.

images.archetype: Data-concept chart (simple-figure Scaffold D) — conceptual, not patient data
images.section: Clinician tab · "Symptomatic hyponatremia: protocol, target and ceiling" (#md-hypo-emerg)
images.alt: Chart of sodium over 48 hours: two early boluses reach a +4 to 6 target band; later a water diuresis between blood draws pushes sodium past the 8 mmol/L ceiling of a rolling 24-hour window.
Five triggers that can start a water diuresis feed into a sodium timeline marking proactive, reactive and rescue desmopressin strategies.

images.archetype: Stepwise ladder / wide algorithm (algorithm-generator Mode C, landscape)
images.section: Clinician tab · "Treat the cause → SIAD stepwise" (#md-cause)
images.alt: A four-step staircase for SIAD: treat the cause and nutrition, restrict all fluids, check the urine electrolyte ratio, then compare urea and tolvaptan, with empagliflozin marked investigational.

images.section: Clinician tab · "Hypernatremia: diagnose the loss, replace the water" (#md-hyper)
images.alt: A water tank below its fill line with an open drain shows that replacing hypernatremia needs the missing water plus ongoing losses, after perfusion is restored, with sodium rechecked every few hours.

images.archetype: Multi-panel patient infographic with photorealistic Filipino vignettes (infographic-skill archetype 4)
images.section: Patient tab · "Everyday habits that affect sodium (Philippine setting)" (#home)
images.alt: Six everyday Philippine scenes — a fluid-limit bottle with soup and coffee, crackers and coffee replacing a meal, a beer session with little food, a medicine check for water pills, an older adult offered water on a hot day, and oral rehydration during diarrhea.

images.archetype: Biomedical mechanism figure (organ → magnified collecting-duct cell → drug sites)
images.section: Clinician tab · "Physiology that decides every step" (#md-physiology)
images.alt: Collecting-duct principal cell: vasopressin binds the V2 receptor on the blood side, aquaporin-2 channels move to the urine side and water returns to the blood; desmopressin activates, tolvaptan blocks, and urea carries water out in the urine.
